objective: Implement the governed Python runtime/toolchain/data/AI capability layer required by PYTHON04 without creating a second platform kernel, second mastery owner, unsafe learner-code path, or undocumented production dependency.
whyCodexRequired: PYTHON04 introduces executable untrusted learner code and therefore requires runtime/sandbox/security implementation, not documentation-only work.
The work is expected to span 3+ coupled runtime/provider/UI/test files and require repeated implement-run-debug-retest loops.
Browser/E2E, offline/package behavior, failure injection, security limits and provider integration are Class B responsibilities.
currentReality: Actual learner runtime path is subjects/programming/, not subjects/python/.
No learner Python interpreter, sandbox, code runner, REPL/notebook executor, test runner or debugger exists at baseline.
No subject Python dependency/environment owner exists: no pyproject.toml, requirements, Pipfile, Poetry lock or Conda environment was found.
Current Programming simulations are JavaScript pedagogical visualizations, not Python execution.
Current assessment bank is 384 MCQs with 192 unique question texts / 192 exact duplicate groups; quiz score is not programming mastery.
PYTHON02 and PYTHON03 are accepted and must remain the academic/assessment truth owners.
mandatoryDiscoveryBeforeImplementation: Reconfirm exact main SHA and diff from baselineSha.
Locate the existing canonical capability registry/provider/extension path and reuse it; do not fork Core just to match example capability names.
Inspect subjects/programming runtime integration, shared subject bridge, service/control boundaries, Cloudflare/runtime constraints and offline/PWA packaging before selecting a provider.
Prove where execution can be isolated safely. Compare feasible browser-worker/server/external-runner options against actual repository/platform constraints.
If no safe provider can be proven with enforceable resource and secret boundaries, stop before enabling execution and record a concrete blocker instead of falling back to host eval.
nonNegotiableInvariants: Learner and AI-generated code are untrusted.
No platform secret or unrestricted environment variable may enter learner execution.
No ungoverned browser/host eval or exec path.
Network denied by default unless a task contract explicitly authorizes approved endpoints.
Filesystem access restricted to an isolated run workspace; path traversal must fail closed.
Subprocess/package installation denied or tightly allowlisted unless an explicit provider contract safely supports them.
CPU/time, memory and stdout/stderr limits must be enforceable for the chosen provider.
Hidden official tests/solutions must not be exposed to learner or learner-facing AI context.
Runtime/test/debug output is structured evidence; stdout text alone is not correctness.
First official attempt remains immutable and retries append through the canonical learner-state owner.
Supported Python/runtime/package identity must be explicit for official evidence.
Late/stale result from another task/tab/session must not overwrite newer attempt state.
Offline behavior must be honest: never claim offline execution without evidence.
AI is advisory and bounded; it cannot grant mastery or execute privileged code.
No production deployment from this packet.
requiredDeliverables: implementation and tests required to make those contracts true in the actual Programming runtime
acceptanceCriteria: Exactly one governed execution facade is used by learner-facing Python execution.
Runtime identity/version and package environment identity are observable in structured results.
Untrusted code is sandboxed with enforceable timeout/resource/output/filesystem/network boundaries appropriate to the provider.
REPL/notebook state semantics and restart/run-all reproducibility are explicit.
Test/debug providers return structured results and keep hidden tests hidden.
Package/data environments are reproducible enough for official evidence.
AI tutor is grounded in actual code/traceback/test evidence, obeys task assistance policy and degrades safely when unavailable.
Required security fixtures fail closed and do not hang/crash the app/service.
Desktop/mobile learner journeys and relevant offline/failure paths pass browser acceptance.
Targeted static + unit/integration + browser/E2E + security/failure-injection regressions pass at one exact head SHA.
PYTHON04 evidence/state records the exact tested head and produces a stable PYTHON05 input contract.
executionProtocol: Inspect -> choose canonical owner/provider -> write/update contracts -> smallest safe implementation -> targeted tests -> failure injection -> browser/E2E -> regression -> record exact evidence.
Fix root causes, never weaken tests merely to get green.
Keep implementation additive/backward-compatible until migration evidence proves otherwise.

Do not ask the user ordinary technical choices that can be resolved from evidence; stop only for credentials, external infrastructure authority, destructive action or a genuine architecture/product decision not inferable from the repository.
stopConditions: No safe execution isolation can be proven on available infrastructure.
Required provider needs credentials/external service authorization not already available.
A change would redefine a global Constitution owner, canonical mastery store or production release mechanism.
A destructive learner-state/data migration would be required without explicit authorization.
releasePolicy: Complete PYTHON04 and merge only after full exact-head acceptance. No Production deployment from this packet. PYTHON05 remains blocked until the native provider and remaining work-packet gates pass.

upstreamProductPacket.scope: historical UI/local integration; native/security/assessment revalidation still required
